claims.text: In Đơn Hàng at stage-0, order_items.order_id references orders.id and order_items.quantity carries CHECK (quantity > 0), so an item row cannot exist without its order and a quantity of 0 is refused.
At stage-0 the lab holds 12 orders and customer 5 (Vũ Gia Khánh) has none of them; product 3 is 'Tai nghe' at 890000 đồng.
In PostgreSQL 17, a statement sent outside a transaction block runs in a transaction of its own, so its effect stands on its own and a later statement's failure does not undo it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, Tutorial ch. 3.4 Transactions, first paragraphs

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, BEGIN opens a transaction block and every statement until COMMIT or ROLLBACK belongs to that one transaction.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: BEGIN reference page

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, COMMIT makes the transaction's changes permanent and visible to other sessions; ROLLBACK discards every change the transaction made.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, SQL Commands: COMMIT and ROLLBACK reference pages

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, a session sees its own uncommitted changes, while other sessions do not see any of a transaction's changes until it commits.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs ch. 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level (no dirty reads)

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, a successful COMMIT has written the transaction to permanent storage, so the changes survive a crash or power loss immediately after it.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs ch. 29.1 Reliability / WAL; COMMIT reference page

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, after an error inside a transaction block the server rejects further commands except ending ones; COMMIT or ROLLBACK ends the block and, absent a savepoint, none of its changes survive (a COMMIT there acts as a rollback; ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT can restore the block).
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, Frontend/Backend Protocol: ReadyForQuery status 'E' (message formats); Glossary 'Atomicity'; SQL Commands: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT; SQL Commands: COMMIT

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, if a client connection is lost or closed while a transaction block is open — including psql exiting on ON_ERROR_STOP with the block open — the server rolls that transaction back.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, Frontend/Backend Protocol: Termination ('any open transaction is rolled back, not committed'); psql Exit Status

claims.text: In PostgreSQL 17, a transaction holds row-level locks on the rows it has changed until it ends, and another transaction wanting to change the same rows waits for it.

db/queries/transaction-place-order.sql at stage-0 prints orders_before 12, orders_inside_transaction 13 and orders_after_rollback 12 against the seeded lab; each SELECT count(*) returns the number of rows orders holds at that moment.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: db/queries/transaction-place-order.sql + db/seed.sql; run scripts/sql/run-query.sh transaction-place-order

claims.text: scripts/sql/run-query.sh runs the file with psql ON_ERROR_STOP=on, so a run stops at the first refused statement; hence if the file ended in COMMIT, its next run would print orders_before 13 and stop at the INSERT of order 13 (duplicate primary key orders.id).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang@stage-0: scripts/sql/run-query.sh; db/schema.sql (orders.id PRIMARY KEY); PostgreSQL 17 docs psql ON_ERROR_STOP

claims.text: Grouping many small writes into one transaction reduces how often the database must write to permanent storage, so the group can finish sooner than the same writes one at a time; the gain comes from the number of writes, so a block around one write is no faster.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs ch. 14.4.1 Populating a Database: Disable Autocommit / one transaction

claims.text: When a transaction must stay open while something outside the database is awaited, every other transaction that wants to change those rows waits for it (a transaction that only reads them is answered at once); keep the block short instead.
db/queries/write-basics.sql at stage-0 wraps an INSERT, an UPDATE and a DELETE between BEGIN and ROLLBACK.
